correctness.rationale: All 400 complementary disconnected triple facets generate 65,199 augmented faces. The exact element matching has 32,591 pairs, with complete acyclicity on 519,792 incidences. The ordinary Morse CW model has one cell in degree 0, sixteen in degree 11, and one in degree 12. Its signed top boundary vector (0,0,0,0,-2,2,2,-2,-2,2,-2,0,0,0,0,-2) has gcd two, yielding one degree-two Moore space plus fifteen 11-spheres by the integral Hurewicz theorem and basis changes. Independent Smith computation on the dual 105x160 integral matrix gives 104 factors 1 and one factor 2. Executable scripts and exact outputs accompany the finding.

originality.rationale: The graph-specific, ordinary three-cut homotopy classification was not found under graph, Alexander-dual, torsion or Moore-space terminology in the searched record. Inapplicability of edge-disjoint-square results is mathematical: the Clebsch graph has 40 squares, each of its 40 edges belongs to four squares. The closest same-graph published projective-plane result concerns the scale-two Čech nerve of radius-one balls, not this cut complex; it has 16 facets of size 6 instead of 400 facets of size 13. Broad graph-cut papers discuss different families and constructions. Residual possibility of unindexed equivalent work is recorded.
residual_risks: Search and source access do not rule out an unindexed equivalent result under alternative combinatorial nomenclature.
Published sources can be extended or corrected later; no independent external audit of the new proof has been performed.

value.rationale: A canonical highly symmetric strongly regular graph with extensive overlapping 4-cycles yields a genuine integral Moore-space summand in its natural ordinary three-cut complex, in contrast to torsionfree wedge theorems under edge-disjoint C4 hypotheses. This is a structural obstruction to shellability and extending a natural theorem, and determines a complete homotopy type, not an arbitrary parameter slice or isolated numerical value.
